newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - June 11.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - June 11.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Dull trading left most lumber prices flat to lower through Tuesday, Random Lengths said in its midweek update. Many traders, noting decent consumption, continued to blame overproduction for the weakening price trend. But they also took notice of several supply-side developments, the agency said.
These included upcoming seasonal curtailments, the fact some Canadian mills had filled April-June quota allotments, and testy labor talks going on in British Columbia, Random Lengths said.
Plywood prices were strong on continued steady demand through Tuesday; most OSB prices held but the sales quieted.

Western S-P-F mills gave ground on prices to keep wood moving but some buyers were more willing to replace at the lower levels. Trading picked up early Tuesday on news of a bounce in futures, then quieted later in the day. A number of B.C. mills who received individual fee-free allotments for year two of the U.S. lumber agreement said volumes were down on last year.
Eastern S-P-F trading remained lackluster. Orders and inquiries were mostly for highly mixed and specified loads. Mill prices drifted into a wide range, covering $15-20 on some items.
In the East, the #1&2 2x4 was the most vulnerable to counters and the lower grades incrasingly difficult to sell. Studs perked up in the Great Lakes region, Random Lengths said.

Southern Pine mills, convinced last week's quicker sales pace was a sign that a bottom was near, were more resistant to counters. But prices gave ground on most items, with #2 2x6 the exception westside and central. Trucks and railcars were tight.
Inland mill producers lowered quotes or opened to counters.

Most wides in the Inland region were susceptible to cuts. Hem-Fir Std&Btr 2x4 grew increasingly vulnerable. The #2&Btr 2x6 held in the Inland and rose in northern California. Prices of 12-inch Ponderosa Pine boards were unchanged at most mills.

Coast Hem-Fir and dry Douglas fir price drops accelerated. Buildups at some mills forced deep price cutting and others opened to good-sized counters to move volume. Hem-Fir fell $3-10 while fir prices fell $5-15. Blocks of Hem-Fir #2&Btr 2x6 and 2x8 traded considerably below published prices. Studs eased down $2-3 in both species, Random Lengths said.

Southern Pine plywood markets were quiet, although some traders reported better activity late Tuesday. Prices were mostly flat but some mills raised quotes. Secondaries offered quicker shipments than mills but reportedly held light inventories, the agency said.

Western plywood sheathing and underlayment prices held firm or moved higher as wood available for June shipment grew scarce. Sales from distribution yards were brisk while wholesalers easily sold recent purchases and held light inventories. Early week sales of CDX were weighted toward the thick panels. The 23/32-inch underlayment rose to about $545, it said.

OSB trading was uneventful early on but prices in most regions held on the strength of order files at least into next week. Two-tiered pricing developed as secondaries sold well below replacement costs, Random Lengths said.
